title: Elizabeth Cady Stanton: 211 Years Ago Today, She Wrote “All Men and Women Are Created Equal”

lines: She wrote: all men and women are created equal.
Who changed the world today? November 12.
Who changed the world today? November twelfth.
211 years ago today,
Two hundred and eleven years ago today,
a girl was born in New York.
She was Elizabeth Cady Stanton.

data.hook:

data.name: Stanton

lines: Her father was a judge, and as a girl,
she read the law books in his office.
The law was unfair to women, and she vowed to change it.

items.caption: Law books in her father's office

lines: In 1840 she married, and dropped “obey” from her vows.
In eighteen forty she married, and dropped the word obey from her vows.
In London, at the World Anti-Slavery Convention,
women delegates were shut out, just for being women.
She met Lucretia Mott, and they planned their own meeting.
On July 19, 1848, in tiny Seneca Falls,
On July nineteenth, eighteen forty-eight, in tiny Seneca Falls,
America's first women's rights convention opened.
Echoing the Declaration of Independence, she wrote:
all men and women are created equal.
And she made the boldest demand of all: the vote for women!
One hundred people signed her declaration.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  Fifty years side by side
lines: In 1851, she met Susan B. Anthony.
In eighteen fifty-one, she met Susan B. Anthony.
Stanton wrote the speeches, Anthony gave them,
and they fought side by side for nearly fifty years.
In 1869, they founded the National Woman Suffrage Association.
In eighteen sixty-nine, they founded the National Woman Suffrage Association.
In 1902, she died in New York,
In nineteen oh-two, she died in New York,
eighteen years before women won the vote.
In 1920, the Nineteenth Amendment was ratified,
In nineteen twenty, the Nineteenth Amendment was ratified,
and American women could finally vote.
Her question for you:
If the rules are unfair, will you stand up to change them?
